text:
zoe: New hires hit a typing error in the sampleapp around cache policy enums. Runtime uses an Enum (CachePolicy.NO_CACHE) but the stubs expose it as Literal strings. mypy/pyright both complain when code accesses `.value` or does `is` comparisons. This blocked today's onboarding sandbox.

akash: Yikes. Can you paste the small repro and which checker/version?

zoe: repro below, run with mypy 1.9.0 and pyright strict in CI.

```py
from redwood import Client, CachePolicy
client = Client(api_key="x")

cfg = client.models.get_config("small")
# Runtime: cfg.cache is CachePolicy enum, e.g., CachePolicy.NO_CACHE
# Stub: CachePolicy is typed as Literal["no-cache", "force-cache"] (string)
if cfg.cache is CachePolicy.NO_CACHE:
    # want enum identity check, mypy complains: "Left operand is Literal['no-cache']"
    do_something()

# accessing .value fails in stubs because Literal has no attribute 'value'
print(cfg.cache.value)
```

zoe: mypy error: "Value of type Literal['no-cache'] has no attribute 'value'"

mia: Ah, this is an annoying mismatch. The autogen runtime creates a tiny Enum class for cache policies so runtime users get enum semantics. But our stub generator flattens common-enum fields to Literal[str] for narrower literal typing which breaks attribute access and identity checks.

akash: Which is more correct? Literal gives better exhaustiveness checks in match statements, Enum gives methods/identity. We should pick one representation and keep runtime+stubs consistent.

mia: Proposal: emit a real enum in stubs (class CachePolicy(str, Enum): NO_CACHE = "no-cache" ...) so both mypy and pyright see `.value` and `is`/`==` usage. This keeps literalness via Enum[str] subclasses and preserves editor completions. Runtime already has an Enum-like object so this is mostly aligning pyi generation.

zoe: That seems low-risk. Consumers expecting raw strings will still get string-like behavior because str-Enum subclasses are instances of str. But what about code that does `cfg.cache == "no-cache"`? That should still work because Enum subclass of str compares equal.

akash: Agreed. The change is backwards-compatible for equality but fixes attribute access and identity typing. We should also add a small mypy unit in sampleapp CI showing `.value` and `is` checks pass.

mia: I'll adjust the autogen enum template so pyi writes a str-Enum class and the runtime exports the same name. Also add a short docstring in the pyi explaining it's a str-enum and safe to use as both Enum and str.

zoe: Can you also include a migration note for the rare case someone typed `cfg.cache: Literal['no-cache']` in their code? That will still type-check but we should warn they might lose `.value` access.

akash: I'll open a GH issue and assign to eng-ml and devex. Please include the minimal repro + CI logs.

zoe: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3222 — includes repro and suggests emitting str-Enum in pyi.

devx-bot: Issue created: #3222 by @zoe — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3222 :white_check_mark:

mia: I'll take it. Plan: 1) change pyi enum emission to str-Enum, 2) verify runtime exports match name, 3) add mypy/pyright sampleapp test, 4) update docs/snippet showing `.value` and `is` usage. Will include backport instructions.

akash: Also add a quick editor snippet to devx docs showing `from typing import Literal` vs `from enum import Enum` tradeoffs so new hires understand why this matters.

zoe: Thanks team — this unblocks onboarding for a few folks. Appreciate the quick turnaround :pray:
